result.markdown: --- title: "[logrank_test()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-function}" body-classes: doc-api-page page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Compare survival across groups using the weighted log-rank (G-rho) test. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/greenwood/blob/main/greenwood/_tests.py#L308-L501){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python logrank_test( surv, group=None, *, data=None, weights=None, rho=0.0, gamma=0.0, strata=None ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Tests whether survival curves differ significantly across two or more groups using a chi-square test based on weighted event counts. The test is flexible: with default weights (Fleming-Harrington rho=0, gamma=0), it gives equal weight to all event times (standard log-rank). With rho=1, gamma=0 (Peto-Peto), it emphasizes early events where more subjects are at risk. Other rho/gamma combinations allow custom emphasis on different phases of follow-up. The test compares observed vs. expected event counts under the null hypothesis of equal survival. A large chi-square statistic indicates the groups differ; p-values are interpreted as the probability of seeing such a statistic or larger if survival is truly equal. **Stratification**: Optionally stratify by a nuisance variable (e.g., site, gender) to compute the test within each stratum, then combine results. This controls for confounding while testing group differences. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [surv]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Surv | Outcome | str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : A `Surv` response object representing censored survival times. Supports right-censored data (standard time-to-event) or counting-process format (interval-based data with entry/exit times). Constructed with `gw.Surv()`, for example `gw.Surv(time=..., event=...)` or `gw.Surv(time=..., time2=..., event=...)`. An `Outcome` or a formula string such as `'Surv(time, status == 2) ~ sex'` is also accepted, with its columns read from `data`. The right-hand side names the `group` column(s) and `strata(x)` terms set `strata`. [group]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Any]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Group labels, one per observation. Can be a Narwhals series (Polars/Pandas), 1-D array, or Python sequence. Labels can be strings, integers, or other hashable types. Must have the same length as `surv`{.gd-no-link}. [rho]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[0.0]{.fl}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Fleming-Harrington weight exponents applied to the pooled Kaplan-Meier survival $S(t-)$ at each event time. The weight is $S(t-)^\rho \, (1-S(t-))^\gamma$. - `rho=0, gamma=0` (default): Standard log-rank test. Equal weight across all times. - `rho=1, gamma=0`: Peto-Peto (Wilcoxon) test. Emphasizes early events. - `rho=0, gamma=1`: Tarone-Ware. Alternative early-event emphasis. - Other (rho, gamma): Flexible emphasis. Higher values emphasize the chosen phase. [gamma]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[0.0]{.fl}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Fleming-Harrington weight exponents applied to the pooled Kaplan-Meier survival $S(t-)$ at each event time. The weight is $S(t-)^\rho \, (1-S(t-))^\gamma$. - `rho=0, gamma=0` (default): Standard log-rank test. Equal weight across all times. - `rho=1, gamma=0`: Peto-Peto (Wilcoxon) test. Emphasizes early events. - `rho=0, gamma=1`: Tarone-Ware. Alternative early-event emphasis. - Other (rho, gamma): Flexible emphasis. Higher values emphasize the chosen phase. [strata]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Any]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional stratifying factor, one per observation. Same length as `surv`{.gd-no-link}. When provided, the test is computed separately within each stratum, then combined (stratified test). Use to control for confounding or variable that affects baseline hazard but not group differences. Example: stratify by site to account for site-specific differences in survival while testing an overall group effect. [data]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Any]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : A data frame (pandas, Polars, PyArrow, DuckDB, a lazy frame, ...) holding the columns named by the response, `group`, and `strata`. When `surv`{.gd-no-link} is an `Outcome` or a formula, rows with a missing value in any column used are dropped first, along with the matching rows of any arrays passed alongside. [weights]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Any]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Case weights, one per row (a column name in `data`, or an array). Must be finite and strictly positive. Default is `None` (all weights `1`). ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [TestResult]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : A result object with attributes: - `statistic`: Chi-square test statistic. - `df`: Degrees of freedom (number of groups minus one). - `p_value`: Upper-tail chi-square p-value. Small values indicate survival curves differ. - `method`: Description of the test (e.g., "Log-rank test", "Stratified log-rank test", "G-rho test (rho=1, gamma=0)"). - `observed`: Dictionary mapping group labels to observed weighted event counts. - `expected`: Dictionary mapping group labels to expected event counts under null. ::: ## Details {.doc-details} The log-rank test uses the hypergeometric variance for the chi-square statistic, matching R's `survival::survdiff`. The pooled Kaplan-Meier survivor curve from all groups combined is used to compute the Fleming-Harrington weights, ensuring the test is consistently weighted regardless of group sample sizes. Counting-process data (with entry times) are fully supported, allowing stratification and left-truncation (delayed entry). ## Examples {.doc-examples} Test whether survival differs between the two sexes in the bundled `lung` dataset: ::: {#94efe689 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import greenwood as gw # Load the data lung = gw.load_dataset("lung", backend="polars") # Test whether survival differs between the two sex groups result = gw.logrank_test("Surv(time, status) ~ sex", data=lung) result ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` TestResult(method='Log-rank test', statistic=10.3267, df=1, p_value=0.001311) ``` ::: ::: Extract individual components from the result: ::: {#44c96410 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} result.statistic # Chi-square statistic ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` 10.326741954885637 ``` ::: ::: ::: {#ed950d6c .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} result.p_value # P-value for significance ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` 0.0013111645203554869 ``` ::: ::: ::: {#9d79c3f8 .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} result.observed # Observed event counts per group ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4} ``` {1: 112.0, 2: 53.0} ``` ::: ::: Use the Peto-Peto (Wilcoxon) weighted test to emphasize differences in early survival: ::: {#4ffc5d50 .cell execution_count=5} ``` {.python .cell-code} # Use Peto-Peto weighting to emphasize early event times gw.logrank_test("Surv(time, status) ~ sex", rho=1, gamma=0, data=lung) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=5} ``` TestResult(method='G-rho test (rho=1, gamma=0)', statistic=12.7142, df=1, p_value=0.0003629) ``` ::: ::: Run a stratified test to control for institution. A `strata()` term on the right-hand side sets `strata`: ::: {#134c8bc3 .cell execution_count=6} ``` {.python .cell-code} # Compare the sexes within each institution gw.logrank_test("Surv(time, status) ~ sex + strata(inst)", data=lung) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=6} ``` TestResult(method='Stratified log-rank test', statistic=8.5245, df=1, p_value=0.003504) ``` ::: :::
